name: Multiple socket outlet
aliases: double or triple outlet plan mark
summary: Plan mark for a group of socket outlets on one plate, shown by a gang number or stacked outlet strokes.
description: A multiple socket outlet groups two, three or four outlets in one accessory or box. IEC-style plans usually draw a single outlet form with the number of outlets written beside it, or with short parallel strokes on the outlet, instead of drawing each outlet separately.

The number is important for take-off and for load estimates. A desk position shown as a 3-gang outlet with data outlets beside it is a common office pattern; the reader should count the gang number, not the symbol, when scheduling accessories.

The library already lists a duplex receptacle form from a schematic CAD family. This plan mark is the architectural counting form; it does not say whether each outlet is separately switched or whether they share one circuit.
readingNotes: Read the gang number; the symbol may look identical to a single outlet without it.
Check whether switches are integral to each gang.
drawingChecklist: Write the gang number on or beside the symbol.
State switching per gang if relevant.
distinction: The duplex receptacle form in schematic libraries shows two outlets graphically; this plan mark counts outlets with a numeral.
